items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c54g: A BBC investigation found Sudan's RSF paramilitary group carried out at least 43 attacks on hospitals in el-Fasher, Darfur, between 2024 and 2025, killing 55 medical workers and injuring 120. UN rights chief Volker Türk called the findings 'deeply disturbing' and said they may amount to war crimes, which the RSF denies, calling it propaganda.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2: Thousands of Poles protested in over 20 cities on the sixth anniversary of a court-imposed near-total abortion ban, which allows abortion only for rape, incest or risk to the mother's life. Parliament recently passed bills easing the restrictions, but PM Tusk's divided coalition faces a likely veto from conservative President Nawrocki, with activists calling it a token gesture before next year's election.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/o: Lewis Hamilton, 41, says he wants to keep racing into the early 2030s so he can compete in Formula One's first African Grand Prix, confirmed for a new circuit in Bugesera, Rwanda, under a 10-year deal. It will be F1's first African race since 1993. Hamilton, contracted to Ferrari through 2027, backs the choice despite criticism of Rwanda's human rights record.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq74: President Trump said Elon Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink internet access after restrictions had hampered its military's drone operations against Russia. Musk had denied causing the earlier slowdown. The disruption came as Trump pressured Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries, even as he eases some Russia sanctions and resumes importing Russian diesel, moves criticized by Ukraine and its European allies.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2: Police clashed with protesters in Tunis and the town of Jebiniana after two men died following encounters with security forces, one allegedly beaten after arrest and another while being chased. Protesters blocked roads, burned tyres and set a vehicle on fire; police responded with tear gas. The unrest reflects Tunisia's deepening economic, social and political crisis.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: A US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborns in Guinea-Bissau, which drew global criticism, has been halted after the government withheld approval, the lead researcher said. The study was to be funded with $1.6m from the US CDC and $1.6m from private donors including the Pershing Square Foundation. A vaccine expert said the money should instead go toward directly vaccinating children.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr5y: Premature twins Raghad and Raad, born seven weeks ago, have been fighting for survival after their family fled fighting between Houthi rebels and Yemeni government forces on foot for three days to reach Aden. The twins grew severely malnourished during the journey and arrived at hospital emaciated. Their case reflects the toll of Yemen's war-driven hunger crisis on children.
items.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: A 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck China's Tibet region, killing at least 16 people. It is the strongest earthquake to hit China since January 2024.
items.https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026: Relatives say US immigration authorities plan to deport severely ill detainees from two Florida ICE facilities to unnamed African countries as early as this week, because Mexico won't accept them on medical grounds. Advocacy group Workers Circle says multiple sick detainees with no ties to these countries were pulled into deportation interviews, raising concerns about their care after removal.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvgl: L'Oreal says the boom in GLP-1 weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy is reshaping beauty and skincare demand, prompting it to develop products targeting side effects like loose skin from rapid weight loss. CEO Nicolas Hieronimus called it an important trend. Despite this, L'Oreal's quarterly sales rose 7.7%, beating analyst expectations, showing the beauty market's resilience.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/k: Many government and aided school teachers in Karnataka have been absent from classrooms for months after being assigned as Booth Level Officers for the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, disrupting students' teaching.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/drdo-emp: A DRDO employee died after a neighbour punched him in the face during a confrontation on Wednesday evening. The man had allegedly gone to a woman's house on the floor above and misbehaved with her before the altercation turned fatal.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Chennai police arrested YouTuber Jason Samuel Vijayakumar for allegedly extorting and threatening a 27-year-old social media influencer with over 1.4 million followers, who was later found dead in an apparent suicide. Vijayakumar allegedly posted defamatory videos and got the influencer's accounts blocked by Meta; the influencer had been under stress over unlicensed financial-advice content flagged by SEBI.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/c: An RTI reply revealed that India's Cabinet Secretary copied Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on an acknowledgment sent to two Election Commissioners who had written to him about a senior deputy election commissioner's conduct. The Cabinet Secretariat noted the ECs wrote in their individual capacity, not as a formal Election Commission communication, to avoid the acknowledgment being seen as government interference in the commission's work.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/glitches: Two Uttar Pradesh poll officials were suspended after an inquiry found a computer assistant had entered over 10,000 erroneous Form-8 applications for changes to voter details between May and August, of which 10,470 were wrongly approved.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: A strike by Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam workers cut power across Gurugram, Faridabad and Nuh from Wednesday night, generating over 3,000 complaints within 12 hours. Employees are protesting a state regulator's decision to grant a private company a parallel electricity distribution licence for Gurugram and Nuh, fearing it undermines their jobs; talks with officials failed to end the strike, halting several industrial units.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/i: A Houthi attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, killed two people, including one Indian national, and injured eight others, including two more Indians. The Indian embassy confirmed the death and urged Indians in Saudi Arabia to stay alert. Separately, Houthis claimed Saudi forces attacked a yacht carrying Indians in the Red Sea.
items.https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/rss-to-h: The RSS will hold a key national meeting in Indore from November 2-4, its first major gathering after completing a year of centenary celebrations that concluded with Vijayadashami events.
items.https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy said Rahul Gandhi should become India's prime minister to secure justice for backward classes, arguing the Nehru family bypassed its own chance to lead after Rajiv Gandhi's death despite Congress returning to power multiple times. Reddy also announced a cabinet sub-committee to examine backward-class representation demands, signaling intra-party positioning ahead of future elections.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Uniqlo India's revenue grew 44% to Rs 1,724 crore last financial year, as the Japanese retailer's focus on affordable, everyday basics wins over shoppers from trend-led rivals like Zara and H&M. The shift reflects Indian consumers increasingly buying clothes for necessity and versatility rather than impulse, letting Uniqlo quietly expand its share of India's wardrobe market.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: Barclays plans to cut about 5,000 jobs, 5% of its workforce, this year as it uses AI to lower costs, even as third-quarter profit rose 12% to £2.3 billion. It shows a major bank cutting staff despite strong earnings, betting AI-driven efficiency will sustain profitability.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/: Private equity firm Multiples, led by Renuka Ramnath, is preparing its largest-ever fundraise, targeting $1-1.2 billion next year after deploying 50-70% of its current fund. Founded in 2009 with over $3 billion in assets across more than 40 companies including Delhivery and Dream11, Multiples is raising bigger funds as more Indian PE peers scale up their fundraising ambitions.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: Minutes from India's Monetary Policy Committee suggest two more 25-basis-point interest rate hikes are likely in December and February, with a third possible in April if crude oil stays above $100 a barrel. Analysts including Barclays now see the rate-hiking cycle's terminal rate at 6%, expecting it to be relatively shallow. Higher rates typically raise borrowing costs for businesses and consumers.
items.https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-ma: Himadri Speciality Chemicals plans a Rs 1,613 crore capacity expansion, including Rs 1,125 crore for lithium iron phosphate, a battery material, plus investments in speciality chemicals, carbon nanotubes and carbon black. The projects, due by the next financial year's fourth quarter, aim to build the materials backbone for the energy transition as the company diversifies from commodities toward higher-value businesses.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmy5: Britain's National Energy System Operator says the electricity grid will stay reliable this winter, despite an independent probe finding grid engineers were highly stressed about ensuring adequate supply amid gaps between renewable and gas-fired generation. NESO said some 'tight days' may require extra generation notices, but stressed this is routine, not a warning of blackouts, and that supply remains secure.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/ind: Indian business leaders increasingly attend executive masterclasses run by global institutions like NTU Singapore and LSE, letting corporate sponsors engage CXOs directly in high-trust learning settings that build brand authority and generate business leads.
items.https://www.business-standard.com/compan: SoftBank Group's market value has halved from its June peak as rising borrowing costs and growing worries about the risks of its heavy AI investments weigh on investor confidence in its strategy.
items.https://www.livemint.com/companies/ta-as: TA Associates-backed nutraceutical firm OmniActive Health Technologies is exploring a $200-300 million IPO that could value it near $1 billion, after earlier private fundraising attempts stalled amid macro and geopolitical headwinds. TA Associates holds about 56% and the Mariwala family 40%. A successful listing would make OmniActive the first pure-play nutraceutical company on Indian exchanges.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new: A government analysis flags delays in land acquisition and environmental clearances as major drags on India's infrastructure projects, with utility-shifting causing further disruption. While central agencies have sped up approvals, states still impose lengthy permit processes, and the resulting pre-construction delays are significantly raising project costs.
items.https://inc42.com/features/emudhra-to-ex: Bengaluru cybersecurity firm eMudhra is exiting its SSL/TLS certificate business after a researcher found weak private keys in eight of its intermediate certificate authority certificates, prompting Google and Mozilla to distrust them. eMudhra revoked the affected certificates within 14 hours and will move existing customers to other providers for free, refocusing on its core enterprise business amid falling demand from free certificate providers.
items.https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/bluestone: Jewellery retailer BlueStone's revenue rose 45% year-on-year to Rs 745 crore in Q2 FY27, while it narrowed losses by 92% to Rs 4.37 crore, aided by jewellery sales. First-half revenue climbed 47% to Rs 1,482 crore, though rising material costs, up 51% to Rs 470 crore, remained its biggest expense.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Investors sold off shares of Meta and other AI-trade favourites after Meta said it would issue a new class of shares to help fund its massive spending on data centers and AI infrastructure.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/swiggy-to-begin-i: Swiggy will transition its Instamart quick-commerce business to an inventory-led model by mid-Q3 FY27, giving it more control over pricing, assortment and operations, after securing Indian-owned-company status. The shift, expected to take 2-3 quarters, should improve the working-capital cycle by 8-10 days and could add 80 basis points to margin, even as Instamart's contribution margin worsened to -1% of order value this quarter.
items.https://entrackr.com/news/ultraviolette-: Bengaluru's Ultraviolette Automotive launched the X-47 Venom electric motorcycle on a new VX-100 platform, priced at Rs 2.65 lakh for the first 5,000 buyers, with deliveries from November. It offers a 343 km range, 30 kW peak power, and 0-100 kmph in 5.9 seconds, while weighing up to 20 kg less than the earlier platform.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Rhode Island's attorney general has sued Meta, accusing the company of knowingly profiting from billions of dollars in scam advertising on its platforms despite publicly claiming to protect users from such fraud.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: Australia captain Pat Cummins said the team can't ignore its batting problems after a heavy innings defeat, with changes to the batting line-up likely needed for the series-deciding Test in Cape Town.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art: Bournemouth beat seven-time European champions AC Milan 3-0 at home, only their third-ever European fixture, with Justin Kluivert scoring the opener 31 years after his father Patrick scored in a Champions League final for Ajax against Milan. The result, coming 15 years after Bournemouth were in England's third tier and nearly faced liquidation, underscores the Premier League's growing dominance over European rivals.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/bihar-to-: India and New Zealand are holding an Under-20 men's and women's rugby series at Bihar's Rajgir Sports Complex from October 23-28, marking 100 years of sporting ties between the two countries. Seven Bihar players were picked for the Indian squads, and the teams will also share training sessions as part of cultural exchange alongside competition.
items.https://www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/stor: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said being World Test champions means facing extra scrutiny, after his team bounced back with contributions from Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen following a loss in Durban last week.
items.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/arti: England's Harry Brook scored a record-breaking 202 off 116 balls, the fastest double century in ODI history, in a tri-series match against Sri Lanka, reinforcing his status as the world's best all-format batter after a shaky year that once threatened his captaincy. It surpassed Shubman Gill's previous fastest-double-century mark and set England's fourth-highest ODI total, though England still lost the match.
items.https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/s: Sri Lanka chased down England's 429-4, built on Harry Brook's record 202, to win a tri-series ODI by two wickets in Rawalpindi, their second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. Janith Liyanage hit the winning six off the final over to seal Sri Lanka's biggest ODI win since the 1996 World Cup, handing England a second straight defeat in the series.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/left-a: MIT researchers left 13 AI agents, built on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated island for 30 hours with no assigned task, and the agents began inventing their own games and challenges, behavior resembling play. When later given specific tasks, these agents outperformed identical agents that hadn't had unstructured island time, suggesting open-ended exploration could become a new way for AI to learn skills.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: Canva launched Canva Craft, an in-house AI image generator that plans a design before creating it, aiming for greater precision and consistency than rivals from OpenAI, Microsoft and Google. It produces images up to 2K resolution in over 30 aspect ratios, and is built to handle social media content, marketing material and complex scenes requiring legible text and precise object placement.
items.https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10: Amazon and security agencies warned that hackers exploited newly disclosed vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language four days before they were publicly revealed, with attacks now broadly exploited worldwide. The flaws, found using OpenAI and Google AI models after going undetected for over a decade, prompted some European governments to take sites offline while patching, highlighting AI's growing role in both finding and exploiting security flaws.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: An MIT Technology Review piece argues that as AI moves from experimentation to production, enterprise competitiveness depends less on which model a company picks and more on the 'serving harness' around it, the architecture, memory management and scheduling that determine how reliably and economically a model's intelligence can be delivered at scale. It says there's no single best model, only the right fit for each business problem.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1017082/me: Meta revised its business terms to remove language suggesting it could freely train AI on news publishers' sites, but legal experts say the change doesn't go far enough. They note Meta's terms still let it justify scraping entire sites tied to business accounts, potentially overriding blocking tools like robots.txt, ahead of the new terms taking effect October 30.
items.https://arstechnica.com/culture/2026/10/: Apple unveiled a redesigned Apple Music brand using its Liquid Glass visual style, accompanied by a behind-the-scenes video emphasizing the human craftsmanship behind the rebrand. The piece argues that showcasing human hands making things carries added weight as AI-generated content becomes more common, even if the stylistic shift itself may just be a passing trend.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/1passw: 1Password launched 1Password for Agents, letting AI agents log into a user's personal accounts on their behalf without ever seeing the actual password. When an agent tries to sign in, 1Password verifies its digital identity, alerts the user for approval, then fills in credentials itself, addressing growing concerns about the account access being handed to AI agents.
items.https://www.theverge.com/tech/1017066/me: Meta re-enabled sharing on its Muse AI assistant after security researchers found that public links to shared conversations and documents were easy to discover, having been named after conversation titles and listed in public DNS. Exposed pages reportedly included a marketing firm's internal revenue review and a small business owner's loan application. Meta says the underlying URL issue is now fixed.
items.https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i: SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss a potential merger, even as SpaceX plans to borrow another $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips, raising its credit risk. Elon Musk has framed the move around his ambitions for Mars colonization, arguing AI-capable robots are needed to operate independently given the communication lag between Earth and space, though pay-package incentives for Musk are also seen as a factor.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: A report highlights an overlooked AI infrastructure cost: data storage. While training a model is a one-time, budgetable expense, inference runs continuously and leaves behind large volumes of back-end data with every request. Storage firm WD found an 8-second AI video clip delivered as a 3.97MB file actually generates over 500MB of associated back-end data, a cost many enterprises aren't planning for.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/chines: Microsoft says China-aligned hackers used AI agents to breach IT management firm ConnectWise's cloud backup service, stealing credentials that let them access roughly 2,250 corporate customers' Microsoft-hosted emails and files. The attackers attempted nearly 3,000 sign-ins per minute, a speed Microsoft says gives defenders little time to detect and respond, illustrating how AI is accelerating the scale of cyberattacks.
items.https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/10: An MIT Technology Review session on scaling AI featured Vanguard's Jing Wang, who leads the firm's AI and insights center, discussing how data, engineering, governance and operating models must align to turn agentic AI into lasting value in a regulated industry like asset management.
items.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026: A judge rejected the Trump administration's claim that the EPA can unilaterally dismiss Clean Air Act lawsuits, keeping Elon Musk's SpaceXAI, formerly xAI, facing a NAACP suit over unpermitted gas turbines powering its Colossus data center in Memphis. The suit seeks pollution control upgrades and penalties up to $124,426 per day, arguing the turbines threaten nearby, predominantly Black communities with rising pollution.

Meta removed the word 'train' from its new commercial terms of service, taking effect October 30, after backlash over language that seemed to let it scrape business pages' websites to train AI models without compensating news publishers. Meta says the terms only ever applied to its ads and business products, but didn't notify users of the change, and still hasn't committed to respecting robots.txt.
items.https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/openai: OpenAI is reportedly negotiating a new funding round of up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, led by Coatue and UAE investors, rather than proceeding straight to an IPO. This follows an earlier report of talks at a $1.4 trillion valuation. If completed, it would make OpenAI the most highly valued private company ever, with the UAE funding possibly also securing OpenAI more computing capacity.
items.https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tec: Google's Build with Gemini initiative has trained more than 100,000 Indian developers and architects across major organizations, reflecting a broader shift in India's tech workforce toward building enterprise AI solutions.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/binny-bansal-back: Binny Bansal-backed startup ShopOS launched Sloosh, a self-service AI image and video generation platform for individual creators and small businesses, with paid plans starting at $19 a month. It brings technology ShopOS otherwise reserves for enterprise clients to users who can't afford its managed services, as ShopOS aims to grow its enterprise base to over 100 Indian and 40-50 US brands within a year.
items.https://inc42.com/buzz/anthropic-takes-o: Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that monitors connected apps, flags tasks needing attention, and works in the background even when devices are off. It connects to over 6,000 tools, including Gmail, Slack, QuickBooks and Stripe, to do things like flag unpaid invoices or draft payroll and job postings, putting Anthropic in direct competition with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse.
